name: Revenant Glacier
geological_features: Continental glaciers that advance and retreat in rapid cycles of decades rather than millennia
Frozen methane lakes that periodically erupt in explosive outgassing events
Ice spires formed by sublimation reaching hundreds of meters in height
specific_features: Microbial blooms that appear in meltwater during glacial retreat, vanishing entirely during advance
Frozen remains of an unidentified spacecraft embedded in the deepest glacial layer
resources: Water ice in quantities suitable for processing
Methane for fuel and chemical synthesis
Preserved organic compounds in glacial strata
description: Revenant Glacier is a world defined by cycles of freezing and thawing so rapid they can be observed within a human lifetime. Its continental glaciers advance across the surface in great white sheets, grinding stone and burying landscapes, then retreat within decades as orbital eccentricities shift the planet's thermal balance. The ice spires that form during sublimation periods stand like monuments to each cycle, their layered structure a record of advances and retreats stretching back millions of years.

The thin atmosphere carries a perpetual haze of ice crystals that refract light into pale halos around the distant sun. During glacial retreat, meltwater pools in vast temporary lakes of startling blue clarity, their surfaces steaming in the relatively warmer air. The silence of the advance phase gives way to a constant cracking, groaning, and rushing during retreat, the voice of a world shedding its armor. Then the cold returns, the water freezes, and silence reasserts itself.

The microbial life appears to exist in a state of suspended animation during glacial advance, reviving from frozen dormancy each time the ice retreats, hence the planet's name. Each revival is genetically identical to the last, the organisms preserving themselves without mutation across cycles spanning decades of frozen stillness. More provocative is the spacecraft wreckage found in the deepest ice layer, its composition matching no known manufacturer and its age estimated at over sixty thousand years. It was frozen intact, as though it landed and simply waited.

The rapid glacial cycles make surface operations a matter of timing. Research stations deploy during retreat phases and evacuate before the ice returns, creating a rhythm of habitation and abandonment that mirrors the microbial lifecycle. The frozen spacecraft remains tantalizingly inaccessible in the deepest ice, and proposals to excavate it compete with the argument that the glacial cycles themselves may be preserving something meant to be found only when the technology to reach it exists. The microbes, for their part, keep returning, patient and unchanged.
